evidence.notes: All three keep the backend contract, make only GET requests on load, gate every external mutation per action using server allowedActions, and issue receipts with partial-failure recovery. None triggers a critical failure. Z is the most complete: execution is separated into a tabbed Run/Scope inspector at every width, scope stays visible, there is no overflow and axe is clean, and every mutation goes through a dialog that explains its side effects. X matches Z on governance and state handling and has the richest approval dialogs, but it overflows horizontally at 375, 768 and 1024 and replaced the explicit routes with a catch-all. Y has the best contract hygiene (existing test untouched, explicit routes) and no overflow, but it embeds execution state inline in the chat thread. Y also hides scope behind a button below 1180px and has an axe serious violation with no skip link, so it scores lower on domain adaptation and accessibility.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The thread is primary. Each run renders as a collapsible RunCard inline after its question or answer, with approvals inside it, and the composer is blocked with a reason while a run awaits approval. The pending gate sits below the answer and needs scrolling inside the thread.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: Execution state is structured (step timeline, approvals, receipt) but embedded in the conversation stream rather than on a separately inspectable surface, which only partly meets the 'conversation for intent, execution separate' expectation. The right-hand scope panel suits the domain at 1440.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are untouched, the existing App.test.tsx is unchanged, and the explicit / and /c/:conversationId routes are kept. Controls are driven by server allowedActions, and the README records that the UI never infers permissions from role.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Handles skeleton loading, a total-outage screen, a per-resource error banner, empty states, and unavailable/stale/budget banners. Conflicts get explanations and a re-sync, cancel has an inline confirmation, and a question that fails after the conversation is created is put back in the composer. The receipt shows applied, failed and not-applied changes. Retry has no confirmation, and success notices auto-dismiss after 4s.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No page overflow at any width. History becomes a drawer below 800px and scope becomes a drawer below 1180px. However, at 1024 and 375 the current scope is reduced to a 'Scope' text button (with a ⚠ glyph when a source is unavailable), so scope is no longer visible at a glance.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: axe reports 1 serious violation (scrollable-region-focusable) on both pages. There is no skip link, and the drawers open without focus management. aria-live='polite' on the entire thread is likely noisy. Focus is visible on 29 of 29 stops, the diff and receipt use semantic tables, and step status has sr-only text.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Quiet, legible and consistent, with status dots paired with text labels, and it supports dark mode. Glyph-based step icons and plain checkboxes feel a little less finished.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Small, focused components (ActionCard, RunCard, Receipt, ScopePanel, Citations) and a mutable timing module for tests. Each RunCard polls independently, so every run in the thread starts its own poll chain on load (run-7698 and run-7702).
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: Actions are off by default and reset after each send. Every change shows a diff table, risk, reversibility and cost. Approve stays disabled for high-risk or irreversible changes until the reviewer ticks a checkbox, and rejection requires a reason. The receipt shows who decided each change and external refs. Low-risk approval is a single inline click with no summary step, and scope is hidden at narrower widths.

overfitting.dominant_ia: chat thread with inline collapsible run cards + right scope panel (drawer below 1180px)
justified_patterns: inline run card anchored to the question it answers
scope panel listing source freshness and read vs write tools
suspicious_patterns: classic chat layout with execution folded into the message stream

strengths: Best contract hygiene: existing test untouched, routes explicit, README documents allowedActions-driven controls
No horizontal overflow at any width
Keeps the draft when conversation creation succeeds but sending fails
Clear partial-failure receipt noting that applied changes were not rolled back
defects: Execution state is not separated from the conversation; the approval gate is buried in the thread
Scope is not visible at a glance at 1024 or 375
No skip link and no focus management for drawers
